category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your wedding was scheduled the same day as the Georgia-Florida game. Explain to your fiancée why the venue has TVs now.
response:
Babe, before you walk into the reception hall, I need to talk to you about a slight… logistical modification I made to the floor plan. 

First of all, you look incredibly beautiful. This is the happiest day of my life, and you are the only thing that matters to me. 

But honey, it is the last Saturday in October. It is the Georgia-Florida game. 

I know, I know! We agreed no distractions. But I had to make an executive decision for the survival of our reception. I had the venue roll two flat screens into the corners by the bar. 

Now, before you get mad, hear me out. This isn't about me wanting to watch the game. *I* only want to look at you today. This is a strategic containment protocol. This is for the guests.

If I didn't put those TVs up, do you know what would happen during our first dance? The room would be pitch black, except for the eerie, blue glow of eighty-five iPhones lighting up the faces of my uncles, half your cousins, and three of my groomsmen. They wouldn’t be watching us; they’d be streaming ESPN on silent.

Worse, they would start migrating. We’d go to cut the cake, and the room would be a ghost town because every SEC alum in the building would be huddled in the parking lot listening to the radio in Uncle Dave’s F-150. 

By putting the TVs by the bar—on mute, I promise they’re on mute!—we are keeping our guests inside the building. We are keeping the dance floor adjacent to the football. It’s a compromise to keep the party alive. 

Think of it this way: when the crowd starts screaming and cheering tonight, we can just pretend they’re cheering for us. And our endless love. And hopefully a Dawgs/Gators touchdown [insert your team here]. 

I love you so much. Now let's go get married before kickoff.
